intervals.label: R&D collaboration; observatory proposed
intervals.note: The status is proposed: the 2025 science paper says planning for construction in Chile "has begun" and no source consulted reports construction started. The host site (Pampa La Bola, Atacama Astronomical Park) was announced on 12 August 2024.
intervals.quote: Today, July 1st 2019, 39 research institutions from nine countries signed the agreement for the creation of a new international R&D collaboration for a future wide field-of-view gamma ray observatory in the southern hemisphere.

name: SWGO water-Cherenkov array (planned)
notes: Design not final: the home page describes the concept and the 2025 science paper describes the baseline design; counts and dimensions are not recorded.

placements.locator: SWGO home page, "shared concept for the future observatory"
placements.note: Planned placement: the array is not built. The site record carries only a regional-anchor coordinate.
placements.quote: Located in Atacama Astronomical Park, Chile.

energy_range.quote: Covering an energy range from 100s of GeV up to the PeV scale.
energy_range.value: 100s of GeV up to the PeV scale

summary.plain: A planned field of water tanks, each lined with light sensors, that would catch the showers of particles made when very energetic gamma rays hit the atmosphere.
summary.technical: Planned array of primarily water-Cherenkov detector units: a high fill-factor core with area considerably larger than HAWC and a low-density outer array, at 4770 m.

technology.quote: Based primarily on water Cherenkov detector units.
technology.value: Water-Cherenkov detector units: a high fill-factor core with area considerably larger than HAWC and a low-density outer array.
